The nontrivial affine shifted-Hurwitz lemma proves without interpolation assumptions that only the extreme nonzero eigenvalues govern the global sharp exponent. Explicit derivative signs and a strict crossover argument prove the unique gain formula, including distinct-root attainability and the equal-eigenvalue Jordan boundary. All modal initial states arise from bounded continuous histories, and the position coordinate detects the slow spectral modes. Rational three-node-path computations and deterministic numerical tests recomputed critical algebra; infinite-domain conclusions use the analytic proof.

value.rationale: For an arbitrary connected weighted undirected graph, a nontrivial interval-wide spectral constraint collapses to its extremal nonzero eigenvalues, yielding a global closed-form rate-optimal scalar current gain. The theorem exposes a finite best gain and an overdamping penalty: greater instantaneous coupling eventually reduces the optimal decay from a network-dependent peak to the fixed memory rate. It includes a concrete rational path graph and the repeated-root boundary; it is motivated by the exact-rate gap left by general fading-memory consensus existence theorems rather than an arbitrary small parameter computation.
